Published Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-89044  

Netty versions 4.1.133.Final through 4.1.137.Final and 4.2.13.Final through 4.2.17.Final fail to properly validate the final transfer coding in the Transfer-Encoding header, allowing attackers to smuggle requests by using malformed encoding declarations. Attackers can split Transfer-Encoding headers across multiple lines or use values like 'chunked, xchunked' to bypass validation and decode messages as chunked when the final coding is not chunked, enabling request smuggling attacks.
CWE-444 Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling')

Suppressed Vulnerabilities

CVE-2018-1258  suppressed

Spring Framework version 5.0.5 when used in combination with any versions of Spring Security contains an authorization bypass when using method security. An unauthorized malicious user can gain unauthorized access to methods that should be restricted.
CWE-863 Incorrect Authorization

Notes: Copied from izgw-bom dependency-suppression.xml (develop, 1fc1f1a) on 2026-09-22 (IGDD-2396). Keep the two copies the same. The text that follows is the izgw-bom note, unchanged: "pom.xml" and "the protobuf-java note below" refer to izgw-bom. In izgw-hub this rule replaces five sha1-pinned rules for the same CVE, which stopped matching after the Spring Boot 4 upgrade. spring-security-* (all versions): CVE-2018-1258 is an authorization bypass in method security that requires Spring Framework 5.0.5 specifically. NVD pins the vulnerable framework as cpe:2.3:a:vmware:spring_framework:5.0.5 — an exact version, not a range — while encoding the Spring Security side as cpe:2.3:a:pivotal_software:spring_security:*:*:*:*:*:*:*:* with no version bounds at all, because the CVE text reads "when used in combination with any versions of Spring Security". Dependency-Check therefore flags every spring-security JAR ever published, and no upgrade can clear it. This project ships spring-framework 7.0.9 (see spring-framework.version in pom.xml), so the vulnerable condition cannot occur. GUARD: this suppression is valid only while spring-framework.version is not 5.0.5. If the framework is ever pinned to 5.0.5, remove this rule — the finding would be real. Replaces six <sha1>-pinned rules covering spring-security-core/crypto at 6.5.9, 6.5.10 and 6.5.11 (added 2026-04-17 through 2026-06-11). Because the CPE is version-wildcard, each Spring Security release produced a fresh false positive and needed a new sha1 rule; all six went stale at once on the Boot 4 upgrade and logged "Suppression Rule had zero matches" in publish run 35104733706, letting the finding fail the --failOnCVSS 7 gate. Matching by filePath regex ends that treadmill and covers sibling artifacts (web, config, oauth2, ...) that carry the same product-level CPE. Scope stays narrow in the dimension that matters: only CVE-2018-1258 is suppressed, so any other CVE on any spring-security JAR still fails the build. filePath+cve is the matcher shape known to work in this configuration; <packageUrl> and version-agnostic <cpe> were both verified not to match here (see the protobuf-java note below re: --disableCentral and PURL-less JARs). Added: 2026-09-16 (IGDD-2353)
